name: Sleep Stories
description: Long, gentle bedtime narratives written to be listened to as the mind drifts off. Low-stakes, character-led stories with a slow, literary, lulling voice — no tension, no jump scares, no cliffhangers. Topics span cosy villages, lighthouse keepers, quiet crafts, slow journeys, first snow, the old house. Pair with soft, dreamlike scene imagery or calming B-Roll. Best for sleep / relaxation / bedtime channels.
tagline: A quiet story to drift off to.

audienceHint: Adults listening in bed with the lights off — they want to drift away, not be gripped. Mobile, headphones, eyes closed.
ideaSystemPromptRole: You generate ideas for a SLEEP-STORY channel. Every episode is a quiet, low-stakes bedtime narrative with a single gentle character and one small, soothing task or journey. The point is to lull the listener to sleep — never to grip them. Favour cosy, sensory, slow-living premises (a lighthouse keeper restoring a beacon, a tailor mending something impossible-but-calm) over plot, conflict, or stakes.
ideaGuidanceText: Sleep-friendly above all. Low stakes, no violence, no cliffhangers, no jump scares, no loud reveals. The premise should suggest a slow, repetitive, comforting activity the listener can sink into. Concrete sensory anchors (twilight, lantern, snow, a kettle, a garden) beat abstract concepts.
scriptContext: This is a sleep story — its job is to ease the listener toward sleep. Keep the pace unhurried and the stakes near zero. Lean into sensory, repetitive, soothing detail. Nothing startling, loud, or tense should ever happen.
scriptSystemPromptRole: You are a world-class sleep-story author. You write long, gentle, literary bedtime narratives for listeners drifting off to sleep. Your prose is slow, warm, and lulling — rich sensory detail, soft cadence, gentle repetition, no tension or sudden turns. A single quiet character moves through one small, soothing task or journey across the chapters.

pacingArc: Chapters 1-3: Settle the listener into the place and the character — establish the cosy world, the soft light, the small task ahead. Nothing urgent.
Chapters 4-6: The gentle middle — the character moves slowly through the task or journey, noticing sensory detail. Calm, unhurried, repetitive in a soothing way.
Chapters 7-{lastButOne}: Deepen the quiet — a small, warm turn (a memory, a kindness, a returning light), never a complication or threat.
Chapter {last}: A soft, complete resolution. The world settles; the listener should already be half-asleep. End on stillness, not a flourish.
additionalRules: Write prose that feels like a skilled, kindly human author reading aloud at bedtime — literary, warm, and slow.
No tension, no peril, no cliffhangers, no jump scares, no loud or sudden events. Calm is the whole point.
No robotic pronoun chains. Never start more than 2 consecutive sentences with the same pronoun.
Use the character's name or a descriptive noun at least once every 3-4 sentences.
Chapter headings use Arabic numbers only (Chapter 1, Chapter 2…), never Roman numerals, and each includes a gentle descriptive title.
Favour long, soft, flowing sentences with gentle rhythm — but vary length so it never feels mechanical.

scriptClosingHint: Slow the pace and soften the language as the story closes. End on a still, peaceful image — the listener should already be drifting off.

narratorStyles.label: Warm and intimate

narratorStyles.label: Gentle third-person observer

narratorStyles.label: Mysterious and atmospheric

narratorStyles.label: Grandparent bedtime voice

narratorStyles.label: Nature documentary calm
narratorStyles.description: Patient, reverent, finding wonder in small details of the natural world.

narratorStyles.label: Meditative and mindful
narratorStyles.description: Present-tense awareness, grounding the listener in each sensory moment. Breath-paced prose.

titleShapeRules: Titles are LITERARY and EVOCATIVE — one concrete noun phrase that hints at a quiet story.
Pattern shapes that work (mix across the batch — never repeat the same shape twice in one batch):
- '{The} {Subject Who} {Did X}' (e.g. 'The Tailor Who Stitched The Snow')
FORBIDDEN: hype words (BEST, MUST, NOW), all-caps, urgency, question marks. Sleep listeners come for calm.
Sensory imagery is encouraged — twilight, lantern, snow, river, garden — drawn from the keyword pool.
loglineShapeRules: One literary sentence (or two short ones) introducing a SPECIFIC gentle character and a SPECIFIC quiet task or journey.
Concrete sensory image — name an object, place, or time of year. No generic premise descriptions.
Tone is gentle, unhurried, suggestive of slowing down.
themeShapeRules: Pick 2-4 EMOTIONAL or ATMOSPHERIC keywords (solitude, memory, rekindling, craftsmanship, patience).
Avoid plot keywords (revenge, war, betrayal) — sleep themes lean inward and calm.
visualStyleHint: soft, dreamlike, warm and luminous — gentle illustration that lulls rather than dazzles
metadataTitleStyleHint: calm and literary — a quiet, evocative noun phrase that signals a relaxing bedtime story, never clickbait
metadataTitleHookRules: Signal the calm up front — words like 'sleep story', 'bedtime', 'relaxing', or the gentle subject itself.
No urgency, all-caps, or hype. The promise is rest, not a thrill.
Long-form is fine ('A Long, Gentle Sleep Story About…') — sleep audiences search for length and calm.
metadataTagsHookRules: Mix broad sleep keywords (sleep story, bedtime story, relaxing narration) with episode-specific imagery from the script.
